###### Cost to design a new vehicle based on preexisting chassis [is about $1 billion](http://www.autoblog.com/2010/07/27/why-does-it-cost-so-much-for-automakers-to-develop-new-models/). Scaled down for the price of a Tomcar vs the average price of a new car ($8,000 vs [$32,000](https://www.google.com/search?q=cost+to+develop+a+new+car&ie=utf-8&oe=utf-8#q=average+price+of+a+car)), that's $250 million to design a vehicle the approximate price/size of a Tomcar. But that's to design an entire vehicle, not just armor plating for it. The value of a car's body [is about 25% of its total value](http://image.slidesharecdn.com/naacampresentation26-01-11-110131021859-phpapp01/95/opportunities-for-localising-automotive-components-4-728.jpg?cb=1296440647), being conservative (since armor is more complicated than a normal body) let's say 30% of it's total development cost is spent developing the body, which brings us to $75 million.

###### Total base costs: $37.5 million each in R&D, $1500 per vehicle in material costs, +300 lbs vehicle weight.
